spec.description: Circle with P at top, Q at lower right, T at lower left and S at upper left. Chords PT and SQ intersect at M. Chords ST and PQ carry matching parallel arrows. θ marks ∠STP.
spec.answerVisibility: All original givens/point identities retained, no computed student values or added proof segments.

children.label: i
children.prompt: Prove that $\angle P=\angle Q=\angle S=\angle T$.

answer.worked: Angles PQS and PTS stand on chord PS, so $\angle Q=\angle T=\theta$. Since $PQ\parallel ST$, alternate angles on PT give $\angle P=\angle T=\theta$. Angles TPQ and TSQ stand on chord TQ, so $\angle S=\angle P=\theta$. Hence all four drawn angles are equal.
In triangle PMQ, the equal base angles from part i give $PM=QM$. In triangle SMT they give $SM=TM$. Since M lies inside both PT and SQ, adding these equal lengths gives $PT=PM+MT=QM+MS=SQ$.

spec.description: Circle with G at top, P at upper left, Q at upper right and R at bottom. Draw GP, GQ, PQ, PR and QR. GP and GQ have matching triple ticks; PQ, PR and QR have matching double ticks. α = ∠QPR, β = ∠PGQ and γ = ∠GPQ. G and R have red point markers.
spec.answerVisibility: All original givens/point identities retained, no computed student values or added proof segments.

answer.worked: The three double-marked sides make PQR equilateral, so $\alpha=60^\circ$. Opposite angles in cyclic PGQR are supplementary, so $\beta=180^\circ-60^\circ=120^\circ$. Since GP=GQ, triangle PGQ is isosceles and $\gamma=\frac{(180^\circ-120^\circ)}{2}=30^\circ$.

answer.short: The angle where GR meets PQ is $90^\circ$.
answer.worked: Join GR and let M be its intersection with PQ. Angles GRP and GQP stand on chord GP, and angles GRQ and GPQ stand on chord GQ, so both angles at R are $30^\circ$. In triangle PMR, $\angle MPR=60^\circ$ and $\angle PRM=30^\circ$. Thus $\angle PMR=180^\circ-60^\circ-30^\circ=90^\circ$, proving $PQ\perp GR$.
